title: AI Red-Teaming Standards — NIST ARIA vs UK AISI Framework: Convergence for Cross-Jurisdiction Compliance
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle — NIST AI 600-1 (GenAI Profile) finalised July 2026; UK AISI evaluation framework active since May 2026; both mandate structured red-teaming for frontier models; cross-jurisdiction operators need a single audit-grade test regime
body: Two major AI red-teaming frameworks now govern frontier-model evaluation on either side of the Atlantic: NIST ARIA (Assessing Risks and Impacts of AI, operationalised through AI 600-1 GenAI Profile, July 2026) and the UK AI Safety Institute (AISI) evaluation framework (active since May 2026, mandatory for frontier developers accessing UK government procurement). Both require structured adversarial testing — but their taxonomies differ. NIST ARIA organises around twelve risk categories (CBRN, cyber, deception, bias, etc.) with quantitative measurement scales; UK AISI uses a capability-threshold model with four safety tiers and a dangerous capability trigger. For a cross-jurisdiction AI operator, the operational question is convergence: can one red-teaming campaign satisfy both frameworks without duplication? The Council of AI position: yes — IF the test harness emits signed, schema-normalised measurement cards that map NIST ARIA risk categories to AISI capability tiers via a published crosswalk. The verified measurement credential becomes the bridge: a single set of red-teaming results, independently signed, satisfies Article 9 (risk management) and Article 15 (accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity) of the EU AI Act while simultaneously meeting UK AISI procurement gate requirements and NIST AI RMF GenAI Profile attestation. The posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation — red-teaming proves the model was stressed, not that it is safe. The signature proves who did the testing and that the cards have not been altered post-hoc.
